beats.title: 01 — The question
beats.text: How does logistic regression learn? Two weights move downhill, turning prediction errors into a better model.

beats.title: 02 — Two adjustable weights
beats.text: The sigmoid turns a weighted sum into a probability. Here, the bias stays at zero.

beats.title: 03 — Read the landscape
beats.text: Each point is a pair of weights. Contours join equal cross-entropy loss. Inner contours mean lower loss.

beats.title: 04 — Find downhill
beats.text: The gradient points steepest uphill. Move in the opposite direction. The learning rate sets the step size.

beats.title: 05 — Where the gradient comes from
beats.text: Prediction minus label measures each example's error. Multiply by its features to find each weight's contribution.

beats.title: 06 — Repeat
beats.text: Average those contributions, then subtract. Repeat: loss falls, and updates shrink near the minimum.

beats.title: 07 — The reason it works
beats.text: Locally, loss changes by approximately minus the learning rate times the squared gradient length. Small enough steps decrease loss.

beats.title: 08 — Takeaway
beats.text: Logistic loss is convex. With a suitable step size, this overlapping dataset leads to a finite global minimum.
